title: Respite care services for caregivers in Singapore
asked: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked for the average take-up rate of caregiving respite services, whether supply meets demand from caregivers facing burnout, and what plans the Ministry has to improve and expand these services for seniors, disabled individuals and those with special needs.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said respite care taps the capacity of existing care services for seniors, persons with disabilities (PwDs) and children with developmental needs, and that providers are generally able to meet demand, with the Agency for Integrated Care and SG Enable prioritising clients with urgent care needs, including caregivers seeking help to cope with burnout. In 2025, caregivers of over 14,600 seniors and over 3,600 PwDs and children with developmental needs used subsidised respite care services. He said the Ministry will continue to review respite services, and that the Home Personal Care service will be enhanced later this year with longer service hours and after-hours care, including for respite care. The Take-a-Break home-based respite programme for PwDs and children with developmental needs is also being reviewed.
